applied.problem: "After the first cycles, the bigger synchronous reactance carries the current" is too absolute: a real set passes through its transient reactance for much of a start and nears the synchronous value only later, as analogy.breaks says.

Screen 6 repeats the absolute synchronous-reactance claim; Screen 13 says B is motored if A takes the whole load, but B only runs as a motor once A pushes past the whole load (at exactly the whole load B carries none).

The worked example states 0.15 per unit as fact though it is an example value; "a start is mostly kVA" is not meaningful since kW is part of kVA; "one at a time needs much less" generalises one worked case of 40%.

notes.problem: The research differs on which reactance sets the first-instant dip: one maker ties it to the subtransient reactance, another to the transient reactance. The lesson uses sub-transient only; a fair simplification, flagged for review.
